checkpoint_text:
Step 1: Let $\bold{v} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}$ be an arbitrary two-dimensional vector. We need to find the smallest positive real number $C$ such that
\[
\left\| \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \right\| \le C \|\bold{v}\|.
\]

problem:
Find the smallest positive real number $C$ for which
\[\left\| \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 \end{pmatrix} \bold{v} \right\| \le C \|\bold{v}\|\]for all two-dimensional vectors $\bold{v}.$

Note that for a two-dimensional vector $\mathbf{a},$ $\|\mathbf{a}\|$ is the magnitude of $\mathbf{a}.$
